correctness.rationale: Boissière--Sarti Proposition 4.1 classifies all lines on the sextic into joins and invertible graphs. For each of all 120 images of infinity, zero, one, exact Gaussian calculations identify 24 stabilizers, prove all six-degree multiplier identities, and exclude all 96 others at every p>=7 by norms with prime factors only 2,5. The normalized scalar expression forces all 180 lines into Q(zeta_24), and diag(1,i) gives a primitive zeta_24 coefficient, proving minimality. Exact 8-Galois-element fixed-point calculation and determinant-square criterion at p5 establish every displayed rational and geometric line count. Standalone stdlib verify.py returned VERIFY_OK and independently checked eleven good primes; infinite assertions rest on proved group/certificate arguments, not on sampling.

originality.rationale: Geometric line classification and the 180-line total in Boissière--Sarti are deliberately excluded from the new contribution. The 2024 Esser--Li and Yang--Yu--Zhu papers classify extremal complex automorphisms but do not derive minimal rational line fields or exact modulo-24 rational-line spectra. Searches through published mathematical records, comparison with relevant earlier geometric findings, and targeted primary literature found no exact or dominating arithmetic classification. The complete characteristic-five profile is combined with the nontrivial good-prime arithmetic classification; known Hermitian 756-line count alone is not offered as novelty.

value.rationale: The surface is natural and prominent as both maximal-aut sextic and extremal 180-geometric-line example. The exact minimal field and rational-line spectrum are intrinsic arithmetic invariants, with all prime residues covered rather than selected examples. The pronounced discrepancy between 180 geometric and 20 rational lines, six different prime-field counts and the characteristic-five jump is meaningful for rational line configurations and reduction theory and is not a routine restatement of the geometric line total.
